history.note: React #419 fixed: identity.ts guarded localStorage for the static render; _layout.tsx mounts the route tree after hydration via useIsHydrated(). Verified zero page/console errors on menu, match-lobby, replay-library (classic) and match-dealt (3d); full legacy Playwright suite 103 passed / 1 skipped.

Placeholder triangle overrun closed by the real table (83,522 tris, 11 draw calls). Lighthouse regression from the menu backdrop fixed (0.66 → green) by deferring the mount past idle and skipping it on the low tier.

issues.title: Desktop claim: toast stacks ON the ClaimBar, covering the PENG button
issues.detail: The 'CHI · Sora called' toast (approx x 652-788, y 500-550 CSS) sits with its bottom ~20 px inside the claim strip (y 530-585): it covers the top border of the strip, the upper third of the gold 碰 PENG button and the tops of the three preview tiles (zoom crop /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-modern-mahjong/cdc52f96-171c-520e-b412-7b47ea831ea7/scratchpad/c1-desktop-claim-toast.png). This is HUD-over-HUD on the primary CTA during a claim window. The report says the toast is 'stacked above' the strip, but the stack has no gap — the toast is anchored to the band centre, not to the strip's measured top. Fix: anchor the toast bottom = ClaimBar top − 8 px using the strip's measured layout height (or the same HudRects band top), and clamp so the toast never intersects the strip rect; alternatively reuse the landscape solution and put the desktop toast in the chrome row next to the far seat badge (there is ample room at 1440 px).

issues.title: Landscape ClaimBar lies on the near wall's tile backs
issues.detail: The 56 px ClaimBar (x ~325-590, y ~195-250 CSS) overlaps the near wall's blue tops by ~12 CSS px along its entire bottom edge in match-claim (full 17-stack near wall) and the first three stacks in match-mid-hand (crop c8-landscape-claim-strip.png). It reads as a panel dropped onto the wall rather than floating in a felt band; the engineer disclosed it as a known gap but it is exactly the 'HUD never overlaps tiles' rule. Fix options: (a) when band < strip height + 8, switch to a 44 px single-row variant (drop the preview-tile row and fold the preview into the button label 碰 PENG ▸ 3×) so it fits the 41 px band; (b) own the overlap: centre the strip on the wall row itself with a stronger 0.78-alpha glass + shadow so the wall is clearly beneath it, never half-covered; (c) put the strip in the chrome row alongside the toast.

issues.title: River-zoom header: chrome row is not glass — rail and far-wall tops show between the pills
issues.detail: The seat-strip glass starts at y≈52 CSS; the chrome row above it (y 0-52) is painted directly over the wood rail and the far wall's near-top edge, so blue tile tops peek out between the DRAW pill and the ✕ (x≈208-252, y≈44-52) and behind the ✕/gear/☰ buttons (crop c4-zoom-header.png). The report claims the wall's top edge is pinned behind the strip, but it is pinned to the strip's top, not below the chrome row. Fix: make the header glass full-bleed from y=0 (chrome row + seat strip as one panel with the blur) or bisect the anchored camera so the wall's projected top edge lands ≥ 6 px below the seat strip's *bottom* edge.

issues.title: Landscape footer pills cover the bottom of the outer hand tiles
issues.detail: The user badge (bottom-left) hides the bottom ~7 CSS px of 六萬/七萬 and the sort picker hides the bottom of 西/發 (crops c6/c7-landscape-footer-*.png). Glyphs are clear but the hand looks like it is sinking behind the footer at both corners, and the tiles' rounded bottom edge/contact shadow is lost. Fix: in the landscape camera solve, add the footer pill height to the hand's bottom constraint (hand bottom ≥ footer top − 0 px, currently it is −7), or narrow the landscape footer pills (36 px tall, badge max-width 220 px) so they sit inside the rail gap under the hand instead of over its ends.

issues.title: Portrait composition: ~155 px of dead void above and below the table
issues.detail: The far rail top sits at y≈185 CSS while the seat badges end at y≈97 — an 88 px empty band that is only used when a toast fires (mid-hand/claim). Below, the near rail ends at y≈620 and the hand starts at y≈688 — another 68 px. The table occupies 435 of 915 px and the left/right rails are cropped off, so the table reads as a horizontal felt band floating in a large dark field rather than a framed table. Fix: let toasts overlap the far rail (glass on wood reads fine) and raise the camera band so the far rail meets the badge row at ~20 px; spend the recovered height on scale (x ±12.4 would also bring a 6 px sliver of the side rails back into frame so the table is framed on all four sides and the opponents' racks are not touching the viewport edge at x≈10 px).

issues.title: Dead-wall 0.18 step reads as misaligned stacks, not a marker
issues.state: match-dealt @ desktop (near wall right end), match-dealt @ phone (far wall right end)
issues.detail: The last two stacks step toward the rail by less than a fifth of a tile and the 0.62 tint is barely distinguishable, so the kink looks like a placement bug (crop c3-desktop-nearwall-kink.png; portrait far wall at x≈295-320, y≈238-262 CSS). Either make the separation unambiguous (a half-tile gap between live and dead stacks, as on a real table) or drop the offset and rely on a stronger tint (≈0.5) plus a slightly warmer back colour.

issues.title: Portrait full-table river glyphs are soft at ~17.7 px
issues.detail: Discards render at roughly 17-18 CSS px with dpr 1.5 (perf JSON shows dpr 1.5, not the viewport's 2), so 索/萬 glyphs and the upside-down far river are guessable rather than readable (crop c9-portrait-river.png). The zoom tap remains the path, but consider letting the 'low' tier use dpr 2 on ≤ 420 px viewports (11 draw calls leave headroom), or scale river tiles 1.1× in portrait only.

issues.title: Landscape chrome ☰ button crowds the far wall's top-left corner
issues.detail: The ☰ button's bottom-right corner is ~4 CSS px from the far wall's top-left end (crop c10-landscape-chrome-wall.png). Not overlapping, but the chrome row and the wall visually touch. Nudge the far wall's projected top ≥ 8 px below the chrome row in the landscape solve or shrink the chrome buttons to 40 px in landscape.

issues.title: DISMISS pill text contrast looks under 4.5:1
issues.state: all landscape states with the FullscreenPrompt
issues.detail: The DISMISS secondary pill uses a mid-grey label on dark glass that reads well below the 0.62-alpha secondary text spec. Use rgba(255,255,255,0.62) minimum.

history.notes: 4 rounds: 7.9 → 8.2 → 8.2 → 8.3. Zero errors; 11 draw calls / 83k triangles / 9 programs on every state. Merged into integration; open issues carried forward.

issues.title: Desktop: dice pair straddles the Tutorial card's top-right corner
issues.detail: At 1440x900 the hero dice sit at roughly (1215-1275, 305-355) CSS px while the Tutorial GlassCard's top-right corner is at (1255, 343). The zoomed crop shows one die half behind the glass (blurred, dimmed, with the card shadow across it) and half crisp outside — exactly the half-sharp/half-blurred straddle the occluder band exists to prevent. The dice are hero-adjacent, not drift tiles, so they bypass occluderFactor and are placed purely by layout. Fix: either run the dice resting position through the same occluder/keep-out test in reseedForOccluders (nudge them ~40 px up-right until factor >= 0.9), or move the desktop dice to the open void right of the fan's 中中 end where nothing is registered. Reproduce with the desktop menu shot; verify the die is fully clear of every glass rect.

issues.title: Phone portrait: drift tiles ghost inside the MATCH CODE input and across the Join match CTA
issues.detail: Behind the Online match card five or more drift tiles are seeded 'deep behind glass', but the 0.62 glass + 16 px blur does not swallow them: a green 索 face sits inside the match-code input right next to the ABCDE placeholder, a tile back overlaps the 'Join match' label, and two more sit around the input's right end. In the highest-attention form area this reads as debris behind the form rather than depth, and desktop cards show far fewer tiles behind them so the phone card looks comparatively busy. Fix options, cheapest first: (a) register the TextInput wrapper and the primary button as 'solid' occluders via useMenuOccluder('solid') so tiles fade anywhere inside them; (b) cap the factor for tiles fully inside a glass rect at ~0.35 so they read as faint depth cues; (c) in reseedForOccluders reserve the Online match card for far-depth tiles only. Reduced-motion phone (which has no drift field) shows how much calmer the card reads without them.

issues.title: Landscape phone lesson sheet hard-clips the third card with no trailing inset
issues.detail: The horizontal lesson rail inside the Tutorial glass sheet has a ~24 px inset on the left (card 01 starts at x 233 vs sheet edge 218) but zero on the right: card 03 'Reading the table' is cut by the sheet's inner border at x 697, with the sheet stroke drawn over it. The asymmetry makes the clip look accidental. Fix: add contentContainerStyle paddingRight equal to the left inset (or a partial 'peek' width so the third card is clearly cut mid-card), and/or a 24 px linear-gradient mask on the trailing edge of the scroller so the clip fades instead of ending on a hard line.

issues.title: Landscape replay library: Import button floats mid-header
issues.detail: Import replays spans x 464-662 CSS px while the FULLSCREEN chip starts at x 807, leaving a ~145 px void; the button ends up neither right-aligned nor centred, just parked at the edge of the 236 px chrome keep-out. Fix: right-align Import to the chip's left edge with a 12 px gap (measure the chip strip, not the fixed 236 px band) or, when the chip is present, drop Import below the title row on the left so the header reads Lobby / Replays / Import as one aligned cluster.

issues.title: Reduced-motion portrait backdrop has no visible drift field (known gap confirmed)
issues.detail: With animations off on portrait the backdrop shows only the rack and dice; every seeded drift tile sits behind glass and is invisible, so the portrait reduced-motion scene is measurably less rich than landscape/desktop reduced-motion, which are fully populated. It still looks clean rather than broken, so this is low. Fix: for the frozen field, seed the driftVisible tiles into the open bands portrait actually has — the side margins of the hero band (x < 12% and x > 88%) and the strip below the last card — instead of behind the cards; or lower driftVisible for reduced-motion portrait and document the decision in ARCHITECTURE.md.

issues.title: Phone portrait: rail corners clip the frame edge and the Live preview pill sits on the wood
issues.detail: In shots/critic-r2-phone/settings.phone.classic.png the near rail's rounded corners run into the preview frame's left and right edges (x~30 and x~795 of the 824px capture) so there is no void either side at the widest point, and only ~14 CSS px of void beneath the near bevel; the 'LIVE PREVIEW' badge (left 12, bottom 10) therefore overlaps the wood rail rather than floating in the parlour void as it does on desktop and phone-landscape. Fix: for aspects below ~1.9 back the camera off slightly (e.g. PREVIEW_CAMERA.position z 6.35 -> ~6.9, or PREVIEW_HFOV_DEG 52 -> ~56 in previewConfig.ts) so ~8-10 px of void separates the rail from the frame on all four sides, and/or move the badge to the top-left where the void is guaranteed. The three-settings spec's 'void below' assertion should then sample 8 px up with margin to spare.

issues.title: Blue back still reads cyan/pale toward the far edge
issues.detail: Measured centre of the face-down tile is #6b9db4 (phone) / #669ab3 (desktop): ΔE 3.5-3.7 against the Blue gradient, which is fine, but the far (top) edge is ΔE 5.5 (phone) and 6.8 (desktop) from the #7fa9c1 top stop and visibly cooler/more cyan than the chip. Plum behaves the same (far edge ΔE 9-10 vs top stop, 4 vs gradient). The single global albedo x0.8 / chroma x1.4 in compensateBackColor over-saturates cool hues. Fix: compensate per hue (e.g. saturation 1.25 for blue/mint, 1.4 for plum) or raise uBackRoughness toward 0.85 so the key's specular lift on the far edge drops; re-measure both edges, not just the centre.

issues.title: Desktop dpr 1 preview shows stair-step aliasing on tile edges and glyph strokes
issues.detail: At 3x zoom of shots/critic-r2-desktop/settings-jade-plum.desktop.classic.png the tile silhouettes and the 五/萬/發 strokes have visible jaggies; antialias:true is requested in SceneHost but SwiftShader does not honour MSAA, and the canvas is only 403x236 CSS px. Because the preview is tiny (6.6k tris, 5 draw calls) it can afford supersampling: render at min(2, dpr*2) via the new maxDpr path when dpr < 1.5, or add an FXAA/SMAA pass on desktop only. Verify on a real GPU before deciding whether this is SwiftShader-only.

issues.title: No hover state on skin chips or segmented controls
issues.detail: The visual language specifies hover = translateY(-1px) + brightness(1.05) over 160 ms for buttons; SkinChip and Segmented in SettingsPanel.tsx only style the pressed state (scale 0.97, surfaceHi). On a pointer device the chips feel inert until clicked. Fix: use Pressable's onHoverIn/onHoverOut (react-native-web supports them) to set a hovered style with the 1 px lift and a brightness filter, with a 160 ms transition.

issues.title: Status pill and Live preview badge use 10 px labels (spec is 11 px)
issues.detail: StatusPill text ('CLASSIC ACTIVE') is fontSize 10 with letterSpacing 1.2 and the 'LIVE PREVIEW' badge is fontSize 10 / letterSpacing 2; the shared language says small labels are 11 px, uppercase, 2 px tracking, weight 700. Contrast is fine (0.62 white over glass ~7:1) but 10 px at dpr 1 is at the edge of comfortable. Bump both to 11 px and align the pill's tracking to 2 px.

issues.title: match-dealt (table-owned) exceeds the triangle budget: 159,938 > 150,000
issues.detail: Zero errors on all three viewports, but budget.violations lists 'triangles 159938 > 150000' on each; the number is byte-identical to round 1 (critic-r1-phone-3d) and comes from the placeholder Table3DShell (3 draw calls, renders 1). Not attributable to the settings subsystem, so it is not counted against perfPass here — the orchestrator should keep gating it on the table subsystem. The warmupMs split (236-676 ms) and the gl.finish() change did remove the multi-second frame-2 stall seen in r1 (p95 2.2 -> steady-state 0 with renders 1).

issues.title: Phone landscape stage is small with ~45% of the canvas as empty void
issues.detail: The 570x150 letterbox keeps both rails in frame (void luminance 0.006 above / 0.009 below, verified), but the rail occupies only ~55% of the width and the tiles are ~40 CSS px tall — legible but modest. Options: let PREVIEW_MAX_ASPECT rise to ~2.4 so the stage uses more width while still keeping void above/below, or grow previewHeight to ~170 px at height < 520 by trimming the section gap (22 -> 16) in the landscape layout.

history.notes: Passed round 2 (8.4 → 8.6). Merged into integration at e5bc1f3.

issues.title: Landscape basics-0: spotlight ring bisects the hand row
issues.detail: The dice modal overlaps the own-hand row in landscape (table-owned), but the ring drawn around it is tutorial-owned and its bottom stroke at y≈375 CSS cuts straight through every hand tile: pixel sample of tile 東 body is 251,248,240 (lit) at y≈356 and 41,42,37 (dimmed) at y≈385. Tiles 六..發 read as half-lit / half-dark with a gold line across them — this is the very first coach-mark a landscape user sees. encloseStraddlers does not help because the hand rect straddles by far more than STRADDLE_MAX (24 px). Fix: when the target rect intersects a large avoid rect (hand row) by more than STRADDLE_MAX, trim the focus/ring to the modal's portion above that rect and treat the bottom side as 'tight' (drop the stroke + feather it the way the screen-edge open side is handled), or move the landscape dice modal above the hand in the table shell. Either way the ring must not cross tiles.

issues.title: Phone scoring-1: card floats 90 px below the ring, notch points at dimmed Rules chips
issues.detail: The focus band ring ends at y≈440 CSS and the card starts at y≈530; the intervening 90 px is the dimmed 'Rules / Minimum faan 0 1 3 5' remainder of the result panel (column sample at x=206: gold at 440, scrim-grey 77,78,74 from 450–520, card at 530). The notch tip lands between the faan pills and visually points at 'Rules', not at the spotlit score header. The keepNotch-over-keepClear rule keeps the arrow but the composition still reads as 'look at the rules chips'. Fix: when the gap is entirely the target's own dimmed remainder, dock snug — top = haloBottom + CARD_GAP — and let the (already solid) card cover the remainder; the buttons below are hidden by the scrim anyway. Alternatively drop the notch when gap > NOTCH_MAX_GAP regardless of keepClear.

issues.title: Landscape scoring-1: ring lights the opponent seat strip and desktop seat badges
issues.detail: Landscape: the ring top sits at y≈13 CSS while the result panel top is at ≈33, so '西 Niko  Bot (Easy)' and '北 Tao' from the seat strip sit inside the lit hole (sample 51,60,52 vs 39,49,41 dimmed) and read as part of the lesson target. Desktop: the tops of the Kai 北 / Tao 南 seat badges peek lit above the panel edge inside the ring. Looks like the straddler enclosure pulling unrelated chrome in. Fix: only enclose straddlers whose centre lies inside the ring, or exclude seat-strip / seat-badge rects from candidates so the ring hugs the focus band (HALO_PAD 8) on the top side.

issues.title: Landscape scoring-intro step 0: centred card reads off-centre and kisses the hand row
issues.detail: placeCentred slides the 'Scoring 101' card left/up to clear the Order/Player toggle: it now spans x 163–601 CSS in a 915 px viewport (centre 382 vs 457) and its bottom edge at ≈345 sits 5 px above the hand tiles at ≈350. The intent is clear from the code but the result looks accidentally misaligned next to the perfectly centred basics-1 / claims-0 cards. Fix: prefer a purely vertical shift or a slightly narrower card when the only conflict is a small toggle, or treat the toggle as coverable (card already paints solid when overlapsChrome) and keep the card horizontally centred; keep ≥ 12 px to the hand row.

issues.title: Progress dots and 'LESSON N/14' label count different things
issues.detail: Header reads 'LESSON 1/14' while the dot row shows 6 dots (steps within the lesson); on basics-1 the label still says 1/14 but the 2nd dot is active. First-time users will read the dots as lesson progress. Fix: add a tiny 'Step 2 of 6' caption beside the dots or move the lesson counter to the lesson-picker and keep the card header about steps only.

issues.title: 3D renderer: targeted steps still fall back to the centred card (known gap)
issues.detail: Zero errors and budget passes (3 draw calls, 159,938 tris, programs 3, idle on desktop) and the dice-modal step rings correctly because the modal is DOM. But per the engineer's own gap list the 3D table registers no <TutorialTarget> rects, so own-hand / wall / discard steps will show a targetless card once the 3D table lands. Not scored heavily this pre-integration round, but it is the next blocker for the tutorial on the real renderer: mount Tutorial3D / setSpotlightTiles and register projected tile rects.

issues.title: Opening-rolls dice modal is a classic cream-paper surface inside the 3D flow
issues.state: tutorial-basics-0 (and every hand start) @ phone 412x915, phone-landscape 915x412, desktop 1440x900 (3d)
issues.detail: The 'Opening rolls' modal (wg-phone-dice-modal.png crop) is an off-white paper card with black serif-ish text, red-pip 2D dice and a grey 'Tap anywhere to dismiss' — the legacy classic theme, sitting a few pixels from a dark-glass coach card and the dark glass HUD. Should be the same glass panel as ResultPanel/coach card: rgba dark glass + gold hairline, uppercase micro-label 'OPENING ROLLS', ivory 3D-shaded dice (or the scene's real dice via a short camera push), gold total, secondary 0.62-alpha dismiss hint.

issues.title: Desktop claim toast stacks on the ClaimBar and covers the PENG button
issues.detail: Confirmed in wg-desktop-claim-toast.png: the 'CHI · Bao called' glass toast sits ~20 CSS px inside the claim strip, hiding the strip's top border, the upper third of the gold 碰 PENG button and the tops of the three preview tiles. HUD-over-HUD on the one control the player must hit under time pressure. Anchor toasts above the strip when a ClaimBar is mounted (strip rect + 12 px gap) or move the toast to the top-centre chrome row as landscape already does.

issues.title: Landscape ClaimBar sits on the near wall's tile tops; footer pills hide the bottom of the hand tiles
issues.detail: wg-landscape-claimbar.png: the 56 px strip's bottom edge lies across the blue tile tops of the near wall along its whole width, reading as a panel dropped onto the wall rather than floating in a felt band. wg-landscape-footer-left.png: the user badge covers the bottom ~7 CSS px of 六萬/七萬 (rounded edge and contact shadow lost) and the SUIT pill covers 發. Add the footer pill height to the hand's bottom constraint in the landscape camera solve, and place the claim strip in the felt band between the near wall and the far river (or push the near wall 0.4 world units toward the camera so a clear band exists).

issues.title: Portrait table reads as a flat top-down band with dead void above and below
issues.detail: Near-orthographic 76° camera, side rails cropped off, ~88 CSS px empty between the seat badges and the far rail and ~68 px between the near rail and the hand. Side walls become featureless white sticks and the scene loses the depth that makes desktop/landscape feel 3D. Tilt to ~62-65° so wall sides and the near rail bevel are visible, fill the upper band with the far rail and seat badges (badges can sit on the rail), and let the toast band live inside the composition rather than in void.

issues.title: Pre-game lobby and replay library are flat dark voids with no scene behind the glass
issues.detail: LobbyGlass is styled correctly but floats on a plain gradient; on desktop ~45% of the viewport (right column below Rules, whole lower half) is empty and no 3D element exists at all, so the step between the menu (drifting tiles, rack) and the table (felt) is a blank screen. Reuse the menu backdrop (MenuScene drift field, no hero rack) behind the lobby, or a dimmed out-of-focus table with the four seats lit as players fill them; on desktop move Rules under Seats and use the right column for a seat preview.

issues.title: Menu backdrop debris: drift tiles inside the MATCH CODE input (phone) and dice straddling the Tutorial card corner (desktop)
issues.detail: Phone: a green 索 face sits inside the match-code input beside the ABCDE placeholder, a tile back crosses the 'Join match' label and two more frame the input's right end — the glass does not swallow them. Desktop (wg-desktop-dice.png): one die is half behind the Tutorial glass (blurred, dimmed) and half crisp outside. Keep the drift field out of the card column entirely on phone (seed x outside the 24-px card inset) and add the hero dice to the occluder band so they never intersect a card edge.

issues.title: Desktop ClaimBar floats mid-felt over the own-river growth zone
issues.detail: The CHI/PENG strip is centred at y≈530-585 on the felt between the centre plate and the near wall — exactly where the player's own discards accumulate after ~8 turns. Early-hand shots look clean, but late-hand the strip will sit on top of readable river tiles. Anchor it to the hand row (12 px above the tallest hand tile, as landscape does) so it always reads as 'your action' and never covers discards.

issues.title: Portrait river glyphs are soft at ~17 CSS px (dpr 1.5)
issues.detail: wg-phone-river.png: discards render at 17-18 CSS px; 索/萬 glyphs and the upside-down far river are guessable, not readable. Tap-to-zoom exists but the default view should carry the game. Allow dpr 2 on the low tier for ≤420 px viewports (11 draw calls leave headroom) or scale river tiles 1.1x in portrait.

issues.title: Dead-wall step reads as misaligned stacks, not a marker

issues.title: Landscape chrome details: lesson sheet clips card 03, Import replays floats mid-header, DISMISS contrast

issues.title: Settings phone preview: rail corners clip the frame edges, LIVE PREVIEW badge sits on wood; Blue back reads pale cyan

history.notes: Rubric visual 8.4 / motion 8.0 / legibility 8.0 / polish 8.1 / cohesion 8.3. Weakest subsystem: table. Zero errors, perf budget met on every 3D state at phone / landscape / desktop.

verdicts.why: B's perspective table with plum tile backs, wooden rim, and large two-row hand reads as a real game scene with depth; A is a flat green panel that is mostly empty space with small hand tiles. A's explicit 'YOUR TURN · DISCARD' pill and bot-skill labels are clearer, and B wastes a large dark band above the table.

A has depth, a readable large hand, dealer chip and dice detail, and a clear DISCARD status pill; B is a flat dark-green layout dominated by an empty discards box. B's compact top bar shows bot difficulty and the turn prompt is more explicit, but it looks like a placeholder.

B fills the screen with a coherent dark/gold lobby, highlights the player's own seat, expands the rules inline and has a stronger CTA hierarchy; A leaves two-thirds of the phone blank and its pale pink selected states are low contrast. A is calmer and its collapsed accordion is arguably less busy.

A shows the whole table with rivers and the CHI toast in its own row without collisions; in B the CHI toast sits on top of the opponent rows and clips 'Bot (Standa'. A's centre river tiles are small and hard to read at phone size, while B's discard row is very legible.

B lifts the just-drawn tile out of the hand and highlights the wall draw spot on a rich 3D table, so what happened is obvious; A is a flat layout with four discards, a giant empty panel and a lone blue placeholder card in the middle. A's 'YOUR TURN · DRAW' pill is more explicit than B's small DRAW tag.

A's zoomed river makes every discard legible and the hand is large; B's PENG toast overlaps and clips the opponent labels. B counters with a clear claim bar (CHI / PASS) telling the player exactly what to do, whereas A's 'CHI Jin called' toast is ghosted and its header buttons overlap the wooden rim.

B's hero of 3D tiles and dice, gold primary CTA and dark theme make it feel like a game rather than a settings form, and it fills the viewport; A is clean but bland with half the screen empty. B's footer credit is clipped at the bottom edge and it is longer to scroll.

A has a designed empty state (fanned tiles, 'Nothing on the shelf yet', a Paste a replay action) and a LIBRARY eyebrow, so the screen feels finished; B is a header, a toggle and a blank cream page. B's larger typography is very readable.

B's angled 3D table with plum-backed walls, per-seat badges around the rim and a hand that spans the width is a proper desktop game view; A is a small flat green rectangle with tiny tiles and a big empty inner panel plus unused space below. A's LIVE/#SOLO chip and turn pill are informative.

A is the perspective table with readable tiles and clear seat badges; B is the flat 2D board with small tiles, an empty discard well, and a dead lower third of the viewport. B's centered 'YOUR TURN · DISCARD' pill is a clearer prompt.

B uses a two-column layout that fits the whole lobby above the fold with strong gold selection states and a highlighted 'You' seat; A's pale pink selected states are hard to read and the page is a narrow column of beige cards. A does surface the match code copy chip and 'waiting for players' status, which B omits.

A keeps everything on the 3D table with the CHI/PASS claim bar floating near the river and no collisions; in B the PENG toast covers Mei's badge and the claim card sits off to the side of the board. B's discards and melds are easier to read individually, and its claim card is bigger.

B raises the drawn tile out of the hand and highlights the draw point on the wall, on a table with depth and lighting; A is the flat board with tiny river tiles and a mostly empty green well. A's explicit 'YOUR TURN · DRAW' pill is the one thing it does better.

A is a complete landing screen: hero tile fan, three balanced columns, a tutorial grid that fits, and drifting tile decorations; B's tutorial list runs off the bottom, the first two columns are mostly empty, and the pastel tile shapes look like unfinished placeholders. B's large 東 tile logo is a nice focal element.

B has a centred empty-state card with tile illustration, explanation and a Paste a replay action, plus a proper page header; A is a blank cream page with an oversized faint decorative shape that reads as a rendering artifact. A's full-width layout puts the header controls at the edges, which some might prefer.

B's perspective table with lit tile walls, wooden rim, dice plate and large readable hand tiles reads as a real game scene, while A is a flat green panel that is 70% empty 'DISCARDS' box with small tiles. Strongest point for A: everything fits in one compact layout with no dead band, and the player's name is not truncated (B shows 'Lucky Drag...').

A (the 3D table) has depth, a clear focal plate and big tiles; B is the same flat layout as pair 0 with a huge empty discard region and cramped 14-tile row. For B: the 'YOUR TURN · DISCARD' chip is a slightly more explicit call to action than A's small 'DISCARD' pill.

B fills the phone screen with a coherent dark/gold glass design, highlights the player's own seat, and exposes the rules inline; A leaves the bottom half blank and its beige segmented controls have weak selected-state contrast. For A: it is lighter and arguably quicker to scan, with the Start button fixed to the bottom edge.

A shows the live river on a 3D table with the CHI toast cleanly placed under the seat strip; B's toast overlaps and clips the opponent list ('Bot (Standa'), and the giant lone draw tile floating in a sea of empty green looks unfinished. For B: its discard rows with owner colour bars are far more legible than A's tiny centre-table tiles.

B has a raised, selected tile in a large hand, a coherent 3D scene and no wasted space; A is mostly empty felt with one oversized pulsing tile. For A: the 'YOUR TURN · DRAW' banner and the discards row are clearer at a glance.

A's zoomed river makes every discard legible with real depth, and the close button is integrated into the chrome; B's toast collides with the opponent list and the layout is largely empty. Against A: the half-faded CHI toast sitting on the felt looks like a rendering artefact and the top-right wall is hard-clipped, so it is the less polished of the 3D shots.

B's dark hero with rendered tiles and dice, gold primary CTA and eyebrow label feels like a game landing page; A is a plain settings-style list. For A: it is compact, fully above the fold, and B's disabled 'Join match' button is a muddy brown and the floating background tiles add visual noise behind the form.

A has a proper empty state: illustrated tile fan, headline, guidance and a 'Paste a replay' action inside a card; B is a headline, a toggle and a bare paragraph over an empty beige page. For B: the light theme is calm and text contrast is fine, but that is all it offers.

B's tilted 3D table with wooden rim, dice plate and dealer chip is dramatically more attractive and uses the wide viewport; A is a flat board with a large empty inner rectangle and small tiles floating below it. For A: player badges sit directly beside each wall so ownership is instantly clear.
Same comparison as pair 8 in reverse: A's perspective table has depth and readable large tiles, B is the flat board with the empty discard rectangle. For B: it is compact and nothing is occluded.

B uses the desktop width for a two-column layout, highlights the user's seat in gold and has strong selected states on the skill toggles; A stacks everything in a narrow column with faint pink selection states. For A: it is very readable and its single-column order (seats, skill, rules, start) has a clear top-to-bottom flow.

A's 3D scene with the raised 一萬 tile and a compact floating CHI/PASS bar looks polished; B's PENG toast overlaps the top opponent badge and the right-hand claim panel floats off the table edge. For B: labelled melds ('PENG', 'CHI') and larger flat discards are easier to read than A's small centre-table tiles.

B's lifted tile and 3D table clearly signal 'your move' with real depth; A is mostly empty flat felt with a few scattered small discards. For A: the 'YOUR TURN · DRAW' chip and highlighted own badge are explicit.

A fits the whole menu including a 14-lesson tutorial grid into the viewport with a strong hero tile row and consistent dark/gold styling; B's tutorial column overflows the screen while the other two columns are largely empty. For B: the large 東 tile mark and cream palette are clean and friendly, and its buttons have stronger colour contrast.

B presents a designed empty state (tile fan illustration, headline, help text, 'Paste a replay') centred in a card; A is a header, a toggle and a sentence over a mostly blank page with a faint decorative background. For A: the light theme is easy on the eyes and nothing competes for attention.

B's rendered 3D table with wood rim, shaded walls, dice plate and large readable hand tiles reads as a real game; A is a flat green panel with a huge empty 'Discards' box and small tiles. A's one-row hand plus explicit 'YOUR TURN · DISCARD' pill is the only thing it does more clearly.

A (3D table, blue-back walls, depth, big hand tiles) is far more attractive and polished than B's flat felt with an empty discards area dominating the screen. B's compact single-row hand and clear turn label are its strongest points.

B's dark glass lobby with gold selected chips, a 'You · Online' seat highlight, subtitle copy and fully visible rules feels more premium and complete; A's cream version is tidy but leaves two-thirds of the screen empty and hides rules behind a collapsed row. A is quicker to scan and less busy.

A shows a convincing 3D table with melds, river and a legible CHI toast, and the drawn tile is clearly set apart; B's flat layout has a lone highlighted draw tile floating in a big empty area. B's discards row is more readable at a glance than A's small central river tiles.

B's 3D table with the freshly drawn tile raised in the hand and the wall break highlighted gives depth and clear 'what changed' cues; A is flat and mostly empty. A's turn pill and seat list are slightly more explicit about whose turn it is.

A's zoomed river with large legible discards and the wood rim looks more like a game and reads well; B is a plain list but has a very clear claim panel (tile, CHI, PASS). A's CHI toast is washed out over the felt and the top HUD pills overlap the rim, which cost it confidence.

B's dark hero with rendered tiles and dice, gold 'Play vs bots' CTA and title treatment feels like a game menu; A is a clean but generic cream card list. B's falling-tile decorations clutter the match-code input area and the footer is cut off, which are real polish nits in A's favour.

A has a designed empty state (fanned tile illustration, headline, helpful copy, 'Paste a replay' action) on a dark theme; B is a bare cream page with a paragraph and nothing else. B's higher-contrast toggle row is its only edge.

B's perspective 3D table with wood frame, shaded jade-plum walls, dealer chip and full-width hand looks like a modern game; A is a flat, small, centered 2D board with tiny tiles and lots of unused canvas. A's explicit 'YOUR TURN · DISCARD' pill next to the hand is more prominent than B's header pill.

A (3D perspective table, depth, large tiles, badges anchored to seats) is much more attractive and readable than B's small flat board floating in cream space. B's compact layout keeps everything in one glance, but at the cost of tiny tiles.

B's dark two-column lobby with gold selections and 'You · Online' seat state feels more polished and game-like; A is well balanced and centered but visually plain. A's centered composition uses the desktop width better than B's left-heavy layout with empty right and bottom areas.

A's 3D table with melds, river and a compact claim bar (tile, CHI, PASS) placed over the felt looks cohesive; B's flat layout has the PENG toast overlapping the Mei seat badge and a detached claim card off to the right. B's discards and melds are individually easier to read than A's small central tiles.

B's rendered table with the raised drawn tile, break-wall highlight and readable hand is more inviting; A's flat board with a few tiny discards in a big dark rectangle looks sparse. A's 'YOUR TURN · DRAW' pill beside the hand is a clearer call to action.

A's dark hero with a tile spread, three balanced cards and a compact 14-lesson tutorial grid fits the viewport and feels like a game landing page; B's light version has a tutorial list that runs off screen and tall cards with large empty areas. B's list gives lesson descriptions, which is helpful but hurts layout.

B provides a designed empty state with a tile illustration, headline, guidance and a 'Paste a replay' action on a dark theme; A is a nearly blank cream page with a faint decorative glyph. A's header controls are slightly larger and higher-contrast.

blindJudges.method: 3 judges × 15 pairs; labels A/B assigned by a fixed parity shuffle, files copied to neutral names; judges never saw build names

baseline.note: Classic RN shells exported before the Three.js layer landed; used as the B side for blind judging.
